subject: RFP: Quantified SLA methodology, latency sampling, and service credit proposal
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@fintechco.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: SLA measurement details and credit calculation

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the quick intake on the RFP. A few follow-ups from our side so we can move the procurement review along:

1) Measurement methodology: Please confirm the primary measurement signal that will determine monthly availability and latency SLOs (service-side telemetry, third-party probes, or customer-observed metrics). For latency, specify whether p50/p95/p99 are measured at the API ingress, edge CDN layer, or model execution completion.

2) Sampling: What sampling rate and time windows do you use to compute percentiles? Is sampling consistent across regions and models?

3) Service credit formula: Provide the exact formula and thresholds you propose for monthly service credits tied to availability and sustained latency violations.

4) Exceptions & maintenance: Define planned maintenance windows, blackout periods, and AIOps/incident mitigation rules that would exempt Redwood from credits.

5) Evidence & auditability: What logs, retention windows, and audit artifacts will you provide for our audit team in the event of a dispute?

If you can provide a short runbook and the SLA matrix by EOW (end of week), we can clear this with legal and procurement.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Procurement, FinTechCo

Attachment: None

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@fintechco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: SLA measurement details and credit calculation

Jane —

Appreciate the clear checklist. I've attached an initial SLA matrix (redwood_sla_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a short measurement runbook (measurement_runbook_v1.pdf) that map to each of your questions. High-level summary below; the attachments contain the exact formulas, measurement windows, and examples you requested.

TL;DR summary:
- Primary measurement signal: our control-plane derived telemetry (ingress timestamp + model completion timestamp) aggregated at the regional edge and validated against a synthetic probe network. Availability is computed from successful inference responses (2xx + valid schema) observed at our ingress.
- Latency measurement points: p50/p95/p99 are computed at model execution completion (post-KV-cache lookup) and at the API gateway for customer-observed metrics. Both are retained and can be correlated during audits.
- Sampling & windows: Percentiles use continuous streaming aggregation with 1s granularity buckets and a 1-minute sliding window. Monthly SLOs are computed over the calendar month with a 5-minute downweight for transient noise.
- Service credit formula: monthly availability < 99.95% triggers credits. Credits scale linearly between 99.5% and 99.95%; below 99.5% we apply a higher flat percentage. Exact table is in the matrix.
- Exceptions: pre-scheduled maintenance (72h notice for >2hr windows), force majeure, customer-induced outages, and third-party provider outages that clearly isolate upstream failure are excluded.
- Evidence: we provide per-minute aggregated telemetry, trimmed raw traces for a 90-day window, and an exportable incident packet (trace ids, sample payloads, ingress/egress timestamps).

Next steps: Karthik will follow up with a brief walkthrough and a live demo of the runbook if you want. We'll be available for the procurement call Thursday.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sla_matrix_v1.xlsx (SLA thresholds & credit formulas), measurement_runbook_v1.pdf (measurement methodology + examples)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: runbook clarifications before procurement call

Vivek / Karthik —

Quick notes after skimming the runbook and SLA matrix:

- Measurement location: we currently report two canonical measurements (edge-ingress and post-model execution). For customers concerned about end-to-end latency we should offer the option to pick the canonical measurement for credit calculations (FinTechCo will likely want API-gateway measurement). We should add explicit wording in the matrix about customer-selected canonical measurement to avoid ambiguity.

- Sampling nuance: the runbook describes a 1s bucket and 1m sliding percentile. We should call out how we handle very low-volume tenants (monthly QPS < 1k) — we do a blended regional percentile to avoid noisy p99 calculations. Add that paragraph.

- Cache & benign failures: we need to clarify that cache hits are included in latency measurement but excluded from availability calculations only if response indicates a cached flag. Procurement will ask for examples.

- Evidence exports: legal will ask for cryptographic verification of logs (signed export). We can offer signed CSV exports for the audit packet; mark as "optional add-on" in the matrix.

I can push an updated matrix with the three clarifications (canonical measurement selection, low-volume blending, signed exports) before the Thursday call.

—Lauren
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Vendor Compliance <vendor-compliance@fintechco.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@fintechco.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: measurement locations and dispute resolution artifacts

Vivek / Karthik —

Thanks for the materials. A few detailed questions from the compliance team:

1) If FinTechCo elects API-gateway (customer-observed) as the canonical measurement point, what is the mechanism for switching canonical measurement mid-contract? Is it retroactive for the month or effective from the change timestamp?

2) For blended-percentile handling of low-volume tenants, can you provide a short example (input QPS, regional blending weight, resulting p99)? We need a numeric example for our RFP appendix.

3) Dispute process: during a credit dispute we require a 30-day window to review raw traces and a signed statement from Redwood. Will you accept a neutral third-party arbiter if the parties cannot reconcile?

4) Retention & privacy: confirm that raw trace exports redact any customer PII by default and that we can request a scoped export for compliance review under NDA.

Could you also provide a short sample run of your synthetic probe results for a single calendar month (e.g., September 2026) to validate the computation? A CSV sample is sufficient.

Best,
Vendor Compliance
FinTechCo

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Vendor Compliance <vendor-compliance@fintechco.com>, Jane Doe <jane.doe@fintechco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: measurement locations and dispute resolution artifacts — finalized items and next steps

Team —

Thanks for the detailed questions. Below are our formal positions and the artifacts we are attaching to this thread. The attached redwood_sla_matrix_v1.xlsx and measurement_runbook_v1.pdf have been updated to reflect these points; I have also attached a short synthetic-sample.csv (included in the Drive link) showing September 2026 probe results and an example p99 calculation.

1) Canonical measurement switching: Customer may elect canonical measurement at any time with 72 hours notice. Changes are effective from the timestamp of activation and are not applied retroactively to prior calendar months. We will record the activation as an on-chain timestamp in the audit packet for transparency.

2) Low-volume blending example: For customers with <1,000 monthly QPS, we compute a blended p99 using: tenant_p99 * 0.6 + regional_pool_p99 * 0.4. Example (Sept sample): tenant_p99=420ms, regional_pool_p99=310ms => blended_p99= (420*0.6)+(310*0.4)=378ms (see sample csv). This methodology and weighting are configurable at contract negotiation.

3) Dispute resolution & evidence: We provide a 30-day window for raw trace review. Exports redact PII by default; scoped exports can be produced under NDA with cryptographic signing (signed CSV with hash). For unresolved disputes we accept escalation to a neutral third-party technical arbiter; arbitration costs are borne as specified in the Master Service Agreement (we propose a 50/50 split by default).

4) Service credit formula (summary):
- Monthly Availability >= 99.95%: no credit
- 99.5% <= Availability < 99.95%: credit = 10% of monthly recurring charge * (99.95 - availability)/0.45
- Availability < 99.5%: credit = 25% of monthly recurring charge

Latency credits (optional add-on): sustained monthly p99 above committed threshold for >20% of observation windows triggers incremental credits — detailed table in SLA matrix.

5) Exceptions: Planned maintenance with >=72h notice, incidents attributable to customer configuration or unsupported third-party providers, and force majeure are excluded. We define "planned maintenance" in the runbook and provide a scheduled maintenance calendar.

6) Evidence package: per-minute aggregated telemetry (90 days), 7-day raw traces for incident packets (extendable under NDA), signed CSV exports, and incident runbooks. All exports include a SHA-256 signature for auditability.

Next steps: Karthik will schedule the Thursday procurement call and share the Drive link to the updated artifacts. Lauren has a final pass to incorporate low-volume language and the signed-export option. If this looks good we can have the legal template updated and send a redline-capable SLA appendix.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sla_matrix_v1.xlsx, measurement_runbook_v1.pdf, synthetic-sample-sept2026.csv (Drive link: https://drive.redwood.example.com/fintechco/sla-package)
